prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused)

Overall approach
- Mission-driven government with five missions: sustained G7-leading growth; zero-carbon electricity by 2030; halve serious violent crime and raise confidence in policing; break down barriers to opportunity; build an NHS fit for the future.

Foundations
- National security: maintain NATO commitment and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review within year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Martyn’s Law; updated counter-extremism rules; stronger powers against hostile state activity.
- Secure borders: new Border Security Command; more caseworkers to clear asylum backlogs; returns and enforcement unit (+1,000 staff); new EU security co-operation; negotiate additional returns agreements.
- Economic stability: fiscal rules (balanced current budget; debt falling by year 5); OBR oversight of fiscal events; no rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates, or VAT; Bank of England independence.

Tax and enforcement
- Close non-dom status; end use of offshore trusts to avoid inheritance tax; close private equity carried interest loophole; modernise HMRC and toughen anti-avoidance.

Economy and business
- New industrial strategy and statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in 3:1 private investment: ports (£1.8bn), gigafactories (£1.5bn), steel (£2.5bn), carbon capture (£1bn), green hydrogen (£0.5bn).
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- 10-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for major projects; gigabit and national 5G by 2030.

Transport
- Maintain/renew roads; fix 1m extra potholes annually; tackle car insurance costs; restore 2030 ICE phase-out; accelerate EV charging.
- Rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; Great British Railways; tougher passenger watchdog; expand bus franchising and allow municipal ownership; integrate local transport.

Housing and renting
- 1.5m homes over next Parliament; restore housing targets; more planning officers (funded via higher non-resident stamp duty surcharge); brownfield-first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; CPO reform.
- Biggest increase in social/affordable housing in a generation; protect new social stock; permanent mortgage guarantee; first-time buyer priority.
- Private rented sector: abolish Section 21; empower renters against unfair rises; extend Awaab’s Law; leasehold reform and move to commonhold.

Work, skills and immigration
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours; end fire and rehire; day-one rights; Single Enforcement Body; living wage remit to reflect cost of living; remove adult age bands.
- Jobs and skills: merge Jobcentre Plus/National Careers Service; youth guarantee (18–21); devolve adult skills; create Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeships Levy with flexible Growth and Skills Levy.
- Immigration: reduce net migration; reform points-based system; link shortage visas to UK training plans; tougher enforcement on employer abuse.

Clean energy, climate and nature
- Zero-carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; maintain gas reserve; extend life of existing nuclear; deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C and SMRs; no new North Sea exploration licences; no new coal or fracking.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), HQ in Scotland; Local Power Plan; upgrade grid; British Jobs Bonus (up to £500m/yr).
- Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon border adjustment; green finance transition plans.
- Nature: expand habitats; three new National Forests; nine National River Walks; tougher water regulation with fines, bonus blocks, and criminal liability.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (more officers/PCSOs/specials); Respect Orders; specific offence for assaulting shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory YOT referral; ban zombie/ninja machetes; sanctions for online sellers; Young Futures hubs nationwide; youth workers in A&E/PRUs; offence of criminal exploitation of children.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist police units and courts; domestic abuse experts in 999; legal advocates; stronger stalking and spiking measures.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; expanded fraud strategy; direct-entry detectives.
- Prisons: build capacity; reduce reoffending via education, jobs, housing links; probation governance review.
- Historical injustices: Hillsborough Law; action on Infected Blood, Grenfell, Covid inquiries; Windrush Commissioner; Orgreave inquiry.

Education and families
- 3,000 primary-based nurseries; review parental leave; unique child identifier across services.
- 6,500 teachers; restore support staff body; primary maths and early language focus; leadership programme; regional improvement teams; report-card inspections; MAT inspection.
- Curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion.
- Free breakfast clubs in every primary; mental health professionals in all schools; cap branded uniform items.
- Arts, culture and sport: creative industries plan; music education network; protect PE; ticket resale protections; football regulator.

Health and social care
- NHS: 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent-sector capacity; workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI via Fit for the Future fund; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; improved NHS App.
- Maternity safety; regulate managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership.
- Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face option; continuity incentives; modern booking; pharmacy prescribing; wider direct referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; guaranteed visiting rights.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict youth-appeal vaping; ban junk-food ads to children; energy drink age limit; enhance online safety; reform gambling regulation.
- Health inequalities: halve healthy life expectancy gap; women’s health priority; new HIV action plan.

Governance and constitution
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; stronger ministerial investigations; restrict MPs’ second jobs; Commons Modernisation Committee.
- Lords reform: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; participation requirements; consult on replacement second chamber.
- Votes at 16; improve voter registration; strengthen donation rules.
- Reset intergovernmental relations; Council of the Nations and Regions; tailored devolution measures for Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland.

Foreign, defence, and trade
- NATO/nuclear deterrent maintained; defence industrial strategy; AUKUS; steadfast Ukraine support; strategic China policy; veterans’ support and visa fee waivers.
- Make Brexit work: deepen EU co-operation (veterinary agreement, MRAs, touring artists), no single market/customs union/FOM; UK–EU security pact.
- Targeted trade deals and sectoral agreements; WTO/CPTPP engagement; OECD global minimum tax support.
- Clean Power Alliance leadership; modernise international development via FCDO; restore 0.7% GNI for aid when fiscal conditions allow.
